title.en: Features prompting consideration of en bloc resection or surgery

statement.en: ESGE recommends the endoscopic features of an LNPCP detailed in the following list should prompt consideration of en bloc resection or surgery rather than a piecemeal approach with EMR ([Table 1]).

text.en: Endoscopic imaging features suggesting low risk superficial SMI (en bloc endoscopic resection) or deep SMI (surgery) [28].

Any bulky (Is, IIa+Is with nodule >10 mm) lesion in the rectum or at the rectosigmoid junction (high risk for covert SMI) without endoscopic imaging features suggesting overt SMI (en bloc endoscopic resection) [33].
Any LNPCP with Kudo Vi/JNET 2B pit/vascular pattern where en bloc resection is not possible with EMR (en bloc endoscopic resection).
Any LNPCP with Kudo Vn/JNET 3/NICE III pit/vascular pattern (surgery).
Any LNPCP with Paris 0-IIa+c or 0-III morphology and ulceration (surgery).

Periappendiceal LNPCPs invading deeply into the appendiceal orifice (defined by the inability to visualize the entire circumferential margin of the lesion) without prior appendicectomy (full-thickness resection/surgery) [34].
Inadequate endoscopic access to the target lesion for EMR even by an expert in the technique [35] (laparoscopically assisted EMR or surgery) [36].
